detail.abstract: AI model providers sell access to the same technology that independent developers use to compete with their official apps. Restricting access may protect official-app sales, but developers can switch suppliers and keep competing. How should a provider set access terms when it can earn from both channels? We study this decision in a model where the provider chooses its API policy, developers choose entry and sourcing, and consumers consider only some apps. Additional brands can expand reach or crowd competing offers. Theory and numerical comparisons distinguish capturing existing developers’ purchases from creating additional brands. When developer entry crowds a rival provider’s official app out of consideration, a provider whose official-app price is fixed can profit from cutting its API fee to induce more entry. If the provider also sets that price, it can instead raise the official-app price, shifting demand toward developers’ apps and supporting entry while leaving the API fee nearly unchanged. When consumers are highly price-sensitive, however, raising the official-app price is costly, and a substantial API discount again becomes optimal. Pricing API access below serving cost can be optimal only if it induces additional entry that raises official-app profit enough to cover the API losses. U.S. App Store records for AI chatbot apps document the setting. The findings explain why providers should coordinate official-app and API pricing and evaluate access against the apps that would keep operating on another provider’s API if access were closed. More brands or a smaller share for the rival provider’s app need not mean greater profit.

Iraq’s accession to the 1958 New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards through Law No. 14 of 2021 marks an institutional turning point for international energy conglomerates and infrastructure contractors operating in the country. Energy projects in post-conflict environments are inherently subject to an acute risk asymmetry: substantial capital expenditure is matched against sovereign counterparty exposure, resource nationalism, and domestic judicial parochialism.

This study investigates how the incorporation of the Convention into Iraqi domestic law recalibrates the enforcement architecture of Technical Service Contracts (TSCs), Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs), and Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) megaprojects. It examines the legal interplay between Iraq’s commercial reservation, Articles 111 and112 of the Iraqi Constitution of 2005, Federal Supreme Court Decision No. 59/Federal/2012, and the sovereign immunity doctrine under Iraqi Execution Law (Law No. 45 of 1980).

detail.abstract: Coordinating projects, working across teams, and planning handovers require understanding relationships beyond formal responsibilities: who people rely on, which knowledge sources they use, and where requests may go when a colleague leaves. We introduce organizational world modeling and the Organizational World Foundation Model (OWFM), a research prototype that makes selected aspects of how organizations work queryable from structured records without reading message bodies, meeting transcripts, or document text. OWFM combines dedicated estimators, a shared personnel state, and a separately pretrained Transformer. On simulated tasks with aligned record access, its dedicated estimators achieve competitive predictive accuracy against tool-enabled language agents, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable. In two independent synthetic cohorts, the shared personnel state supports nine queries and improves four coordination predictions. In simulated departures, it predicts where help requests shift more accurately than all evaluated record-based baselines. The Transformer uses labelled reference examples to serve seven related targets with fixed weights, including two closely related targets excluded from pretraining. Replicated synthetic experiments also demonstrate the detection of discrepancies between officially designated and routinely used knowledge sources. A separate study using real calendar records from one company improves forecasts of future meeting participation over a previous-window baseline. Together, these findings suggest a new source of context for enterprise AI: not just who belongs to an organization, but how work depends on people and knowledge.

detail.abstract:
American government has taken on more responsibilities, but its ability to carry them out has not kept pace. Benefits may arrive late, remain hard to obtain, or disappear before people can rely on them. I call this gap "the competence paradox." This paper explains two sources of the problem: cuts to staff and expertise, and procedures that allow many parties to delay a decision without making anyone responsible for completing it. It proposes a Four-Year Test for governing promises: people should be able to recognize the result, receive it within the term that enacted it, and rely on it for as long as promised. Six design rules and a capacity schedule turn that standard into a planning method. 

The paper applies the method to six policy areas and proposes two institutions to support it: a nonpartisan capacity statement for major legislation and a state-owned National Delivery Service that governments can hire to help build and launch programs. A four-year calendar sets out the delivery sequence, while a Ten-Year Test asks whether the results last. The framework guides implementation; it does not determine which policies a government should adopt.

detail.abstract: Can large language model (LLM)-based government chatbots provide responses, that are equal and equitable at the same time? LLMs promise efficient communication 24/7, yet they may still produce algorithmic biases and rigid outputs. We propose an evaluative framework consisting of two substantive (response validity, informational scope) and two linguistic (emotional tone, linguistic complexity) dimensions. In a preregistered audit of 12 deployed municipal and job-center chatbots in Germany, we manipulate gender, nationality, and requests for simple language while holding the substantive query constant. Assessing 16,921 responses, we find that chatbots achieve near equality among different personas and significantly reduce linguistic complexity when requested. At the same time, government chatbot responses vary greatly across systems. These findings indicate that LLM-based government chatbots can be both responsive and impartial, while highlighting institutional variation (subcontractor, technology, local customization) as an important new source of algorithmic inequality. We also demonstrate that outcome-oriented auditing provides a rigorous pathway to establishing democratic accountability.

detail.abstract: Since the pioneering work of Herbert A. Simon, bounded rationality (BR) constitutes a viable alternative to utility maximization in settings characterized by uncertainty about the possible emergence of novel events, missing information, and limitations to human reasoning. Because of its realism, BR gained consensus in organization and management studies. However, BR is a theory of individual decision-making. Substantial extensions are required in order to turn it into a tool to analyze collective decision processes. Following an intuition by the late Simon himself, we submit that organizations channel information flows in ways that alleviate human BR. Thus, analysis and reconstruction of their structure as well as differential degrees and qualities of individual BR within organizations is key to extend this concept to collective decision-making. In this special issue we collected contributions where instances of BR couple with interaction structures to yield collective behavior. Tools range from mathematical models to experimental settings to computational models, testifying the value of multiple approaches and perspectives.

This paper presents a structural supply-side critique of the draft Heathrow Expansion National Policy Statement (HENPS), tracking how the political directive to enforce a third runway distorts market mechanism design and deepens spatial economic inequality across the United Kingdom. Using Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) passenger and departure frequency datasets, the analysis exposes a profound functional market segmentation: while UK regional airports cleanly sustain low-margin short-haul leisure (58.2%) and Gulf feeder networks (29.9%), direct strategic long-haul city pairs have become subject to an extreme, state-sanctioned consolidation at London Heathrow (LHR), which controls 87.8% of scheduled departures across the Top 25 non-Gulf international markets and a rigid 96.9% share across the top 11 United States destinations.
By evaluating historical route records—specifically the "BMI Cannibalisation Precedent" following the 2008 Open Skies Agreement and the complete elimination of long-standing transatlantic point-to-point links from Birmingham (BHX), Bristol (BRS), and Newcastle (NCL)—this study shatters the conventional regulatory assumption that regional aviation deficits stem from an organic lack of local demand. Instead, the paper identifies an anti-competitive foreclosure pattern driven by legacy carrier slot-hoarding behaviors within shielded joint-venture networks, which treat regional stagnation as a hub yield asset.
Furthermore, the paper challenges the institutional groupthink embedded in the government's Heathrow Expansion Appraisal Report (HEAR). It highlights the economic paradox of deploying state statutory overrides to clear hurdles for an overall negative Net Present Value project (up to -£62.5bn) that explicitly models regional brain drain and corporate extraction as positive national "agglomeration benefits." Finally, the author critiques the anti-competitive mechanics of the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) cushion, which insulates international private equity from normal capital discipline by shifting pre-approval expansion outlays onto consumer landing fees. The paper concludes by advancing a market-driven alternative: halting statutory greenlighting until the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) executes an ex-ante competition test, and restructuring spatial infrastructure policy to support competitive, independent regional mini-hubs at Manchester (MAN) and Birmingham (BHX).

detail.abstract: Reforestation has gained increasing attention for its potential to mitigate flooding, which is projected to become more frequent and severe under climate change. However, revegetation at landscape scale is rarely achievable and therefore, reducing flood impacts with minimum restoration area is important for the implementation of Nature-based Solutions (NbS). This study investigates the flood attenuation potential of strategic reforestation, as a NbS, using HEC-RAS 2D hydrodynamic modelling to provide complementary alternatives to traditional flood mitigation infrastructure, such as levees and dams. Following major flooding of the Wilsons River at Lismore, a targeted restoration project established ~90.7 ha of high-density, native, flood-resilient tree and shrub species across riparian and floodplain areas in two upstream headwater catchments, Terania Creek and Tuntable Creek. Planting locations were selected to maximise interaction between floodwaters and vegetation during overbank events. Strategic reforestation covering ~1% of the catchment area reduced peak flows by up to 10.9% in Terania Creek and 3.9% in Tuntable Creek during moderate-to-large rainfall events, while delaying peak timing by up to 15 minutes. Results showed that downstream flood reductions were partly driven by localised backwater effects, with flood depths increasing by up to 0.8 m within plantation areas. The work thereby highlights that targeted reforestation can deliver measurable downstream benefits and offer practical guidance for integrating NbS into longterm flood management in Lismore and similar flood-prone areas.

detail.abstract: Concrete blocks are the most widely used walling units in Nigerian building construction, yet many structures fail long before their expected service life because of the materials and methods used to produce them. This study examines how poor-quality aggregates and inadequate curing practices, both common on informal Nigerian building sites, affect the compressive strength, density, and water absorption of concrete blocks. Two aggregate conditions (well-graded, low-silt aggregate versus poorly graded, high-silt aggregate) were combined with two curing regimes (28-day water curing versus curing stopped after three days) to produce four groups of blocks, which were tested at 7, 14 and 28 days. A two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to test whether aggregate quality and curing regime, individually and jointly, produced statistically significant differences in strength. Results show that blocks made with poor aggregate and cured inadequately lost up to 46% of their strength compared with the control group, and that both aggregate quality and curing regime had a highly significant effect on strength (p < 0.001), while their interaction was not significant. Water absorption more than doubled and density fell by about 8% under the combined poor-aggregate, inadequate-curing condition. The findings support the view that substandard materials and poor curing practice, rather than design error alone, are major contributors to the weak and short-lived concrete blocks associated with building failure in Nigeria. The study recommends stricter site supervision, aggregate testing before use, and mandatory minimum curing periods as low-cost measures to improve block quality.

detail.abstract: The Crisis of Entity Resolution in Heterogeneous AI Environments introduced four Entity Resolution Anomalies: Identity Collapse, Semantic Fragmentation, Temporal Discontinuity, and Semantic Vulnerability (Beránek, 2026a). The subsequent adversarial reduction developed in Minimum Viable Digital Identity Optimization (MVDIO) introduced finer distinctions, including Merge Failure, Split Failure, Temporal Misalignment, and Contextual Displacement, while also showing that Semantic Vulnerability is better treated as a robustness-related property rather than a realized reconstruction failure (Beránek, 2026c). A retrospective comparison reveals that the original four anomalies did not occupy a single analytical level. This note therefore proposes a non-exclusive, multi-level diagnostic taxonomy of Reconstruction Failure Modes. It distinguishes four analytical domains of reconstruction failure: Referential Reconstruction Failures, Semantic Coherence Failures, Temporal Reconstruction Failures, and Contextual Adequacy Failures. Identity Collapse remains a phenomenon-level concept in the sense established in the earlier paper and is not redefined through the new taxonomy. Semantic Vulnerability is excluded from the failure hierarchy and treated as a robustness-related property whose direct conceptual counterpart is Semantic Robustness. The shift from anomalies to failure modes is deliberate. An anomaly may denote an observed deviation, an unusual condition, or susceptibility to failure; a failure mode denotes a realized way in which reconstruction fails. The purpose of the revision is not to replace the earlier terminology, but to increase the analytical resolution with which failures of digital identity reconstruction can be described.

detail.abstract: Stock embeddings learned from correlation networks or return series are increasingly used as compact descriptors of asset similarity. We ask a simple question: do these stock embeddings outperform or tie with the raw features they compress? We benchmark a modular pipeline (relationship matrix, graph construction, embedding generation, evaluation) across three universes (S&P 500, Russell 1000, Russell 3000), four horizons, six co-movement-removal methods, five graph configurations, and six representation families-including a faithful reproduction of Sarmah et. al.-evaluating retrieval (hit@k, success@k, MRR), clustering (V-measure, NMI, ARI), and supervised readout (SVM-F1) against GICS labels, with paired Wilcoxon and McNemar tests, bootstrap intervals, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction. The answer is baseline-dependent. Every learned family decisively beats a leak-free raw-correlation-row baseline (+0.11 to +0.21 in sub-industry hit@3, p ≪ 0.001), but none clearly beats the raw return series: at Russell 3000 the best embedding is statistically tied with raw returns (p = 0.69), and elsewhere raw returns leads by at most 0.027-0.029 in hit@3. Under a decision rule requiring BH-significance plus one percentage point, raw returns never loses. Embeddings' durable advantage is compression: 16-64 dimensions match thousands of raw features. An out-of-sample peer-hedging experiment shows no risk-reduction advantage over a direct Pearson hedge. All results use full-survivor panels and compare methods under idealised conditions, not live trading.

detail.abstract: This research looks into the methods used by technology companies in emerging markets to convey their artificial intelligence capabilities through public disclosure and how much their disclosures rely on documented proof. The data set comprises a hand-coded census of public disclosures done in the period from January 2024 to September 2026 of 18 Indian technology companies listed in the public domain using earnings-call transcripts, press releases, exchange filings, and annual-report summaries issued by identifiable sources. Each technology company in the sample received one score using a 0-3 rubric for AI-specificity and the number of AI actions disclosed. It turns out that this is a domain where the problem of appearances is almost completely solved, but the problem of evidence is still ongoing. All coded companies have at least one tangible example of an AI implementation, meaning that vague talk is no longer widespread among listed Indian tech companies with active investment communications; however, less than two-thirds of the sample, namely 61.1% (95% CI 38.6-79.7), mentions a deployment involving a client or partner, and even fewer of them, namely 44.4% (24.6-66.3), mention a quantified result. The number of actions mentioned by companies is correlated with their specificity score (Spearman ρ = 0.66, p = .003), and the anticipated size effect is absent: the three small-cap infrastructure companies in our sample score at least as well as the bellwether leaders. Since the IT companies from India happen to be the main source of software and artificial intelligence-based services for financial institutions in the region of South Asia, the research concludes with the screening framework based on the actual pass rate that could be used by Nepalese banks and similar institutions.

detail.abstract:
Surveys that ask adults about schooling usually begin with a filter question about children in the
household. In a national computer-assisted telephone interviewing (CATI) survey of Ukrainian
adults conducted in September 2026 (mobile random digit dialling, n = 506), 33.2% (95%
confidence interval [CI] 29.2–37.4%) said that school-age children (grades 1–11) live with them,
whereas the Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) 2025/26 finds a child aged 5–17 in 18% of
households. Most of this gap is a difference in the unit of measurement. Households with
children contain more adults than households without, and converting household shares into
person shares with household-size data and enrolment counts gives an expected 20–25% of
adults who share a dwelling with a schoolchild. The remaining 7–13 points are spread across
ages. Using MICS data on childrenʼs living arrangements, we expect about 15–18% of adults to be
co-resident parents and 5–7% to be other co-resident adults. The survey gives 23.1% affirmative
answers at ages 25–54 and 10.1% at other ages, so both groups exceed the expectation. We
attribute the excess mainly to the broad wording “live with you”. We then treat all 168
respondents who live with schoolchildren as knowledgeable informants. Exploratory
comparisons show that probable parents and other informants give similar reports on directly
observable events, but the sample cannot distinguish null differences from differences of 10–20
points. Adults who live with schoolchildren rate wartime learning losses as less severe than
other adults (37.5% vs 50.7% “very large”; odds ratio 0.56 adjusted for age, sex and settlement
type), and within these households probable parents and other informants do not differ. We
close with reporting rules and questionnaire additions that would replace the age proxy with
direct measurement and allow household-level comparison.

detail.abstract: Controlled-release fertilizers can reduce nutrient losses and application frequency, yet most commercial products rely on polymer coatings that are costly, variable in release behaviour, and a source of persistent residues. Metal-organic coatings, particularly metal-phenolic networks (MPNs) assembled from plant-derived polyphenols and metal ions, offer a more renewable alternative, but their conventional solution-phase assembly is poorly suited to highly water-soluble fertilizer cores such as urea. Mechanochemistry, in which mechanical energy drives reactions between solids with little or no bulk solvent, has emerged as a cleaner and potentially scalable synthetic approach and has been applied to metal-organic frameworks and coordination chemistry more broadly. This review synthesises peerreviewed literature on mechanochemical principles, metal-organic coating chemistry, and controlledrelease fertilizer technology, and examines recent work on nonaqueous MPN assembly on urea, solventfree mechanochemical encapsulation of urea in MPN matrices, and polyphenol-modified mineral fertilizers. The review identifies gaps, including limited field evidence, incomplete mechanistic understanding of mechanochemical coordination, and the absence of life-cycle and techno-economic assessments. A conceptual framework linking process parameters, coating structure, release behaviour, and agronomic outcomes is proposed as a research agenda, not as an established model. No new experimental data are reported.

detail.abstract: We formulate and estimate a conditional logit model of demand for private rooms on Airbnb in the Mexico City borough containing the Roma-Condesa-Centro Histórico corridor, the epicenter of the city's short-term rental market and of the public debate over its regulation. The borough, Alcaldía Cuauhtémoc, accounts for 50% of all Airbnb booked nights in the city during 2019, and the corridor alone accounts for 42%. We compare specifications that instrument prices using the canonical Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes (1995) sums of characteristics and their refinement, differentiation instruments by Gandhi-Houde (2019). We find that in this market only the rival component of these instruments is usable. The own part is degenerate for all single-unit hosts and, with market fixed effects, BLP own sums are completely collinear with the corresponding characteristics. Both BLP and Gandhi-Houde rival components are relevant but weak, and only the Gandhi-Houde rival set passes the overidentification test. Under that specification, guests are willing to pay 35% more to book a room with a superhost and 32% more with a professional host or self-check-in, pointing to a demand segment organized around trust and transaction frictions. Our listing-level estimates, the first for a major Global South city, are a first step toward evaluating counterfactually regulations whose incidence depends on hosts' portfolios.

detail.abstract: Modern crop production depends on synthetic fertilisers, yet a large share of applied nitrogen and phosphorus never reaches the crop. Losses through leaching, volatilisation, and fixation in soil impose economic costs and environmental burdens. Enhanced-efficiency fertilisers, particularly polymercoated and slow-release products, offer partial solutions, but many rely on petroleum-derived or persistent coating materials, and their release behaviour is often poorly matched to crop demand. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), supramolecular materials formed by coordination between plantderived polyphenols and metal ions, have emerged over the past decade as a versatile platform for engineering films, capsules, and particles under mild conditions. This review synthesises peer-reviewed literature on MPN chemistry, assembly strategies, and stimuli-responsive behaviour, and examines how these properties may be translated to agricultural nutrient delivery. Recent work on MPN assembly in nonaqueous media, mechanochemical encapsulation of urea, and MPN-soil mineral interactions is discussed as an emerging foundation for this application. The review identifies gaps, including limited multi-season field validation, incomplete understanding of release in heterogeneous soils, and the absence of techno-economic and life-cycle analyses. It then proposes a conceptual framework linking MPN design parameters, soil-environment triggers, and agronomic outcomes. The framework is presented as a research agenda, not as an established result. No new experimental data are reported.
